editorial.headline: Data Communications as a Connected Service
editorial.standfirst: This activity covers dependable, secure data communications delivered through telecom networks or eligible foreign satellites, from machine links to remote-office systems.
editorial.body:
Data communications is the service here—not merely the infrastructure behind it. The activity encompasses telecommunications services that provide data communication using internet protocols and/or other protocols, delivered through telecommunications networks and/or foreign satellites that hold landing rights. Its defining promise is practical: connectivity, quality and security for particular requirements. That can mean a point-to-point connection, a remote-host arrangement, server-to-client communication, machine-to-machine links, or Internet of Things communication. It can also support remote sensing, measurement, control and remote-office services.

The breadth matters because the category follows the function of the service. A business may be creating the communications layer that allows devices, systems and people to exchange data reliably across distance. It may support a technical operation that needs remote monitoring or control; it may provide the connective tissue for distributed systems and offices. The record frames these as types of data communication within a communications-system service, with connectivity, quality and security forming the common standard rather than incidental features.

Businesses at each listed scale—Mikro, Kecil, Menengah and Besar—can register for this activity. At the national level, this activity is TERBUKA to PMA and allows a foreign-ownership ceiling of 100%. In straightforward terms, foreign ownership can reach 100% under the national position recorded here. That is the national opening founders should begin from, rather than treating the category as narrowly reserved for a particular size of enterprise.

Bali does not reverse that result. The province’s permanent PMA moratorium blocks Low and Medium-Low risk activities across the island, but this activity is not blocked by that moratorium. At the Besar scale, its OSS risk is Menengah-Tinggi/Tinggi. The Bali status is therefore OK_or_HIGHER_RISK: an investor considering a Bali registration is not facing a recorded PMA block for this activity, while the large-scale risk classification remains part of the practical picture. The useful conclusion is clean: the activity is nationally open to PMA up to full foreign ownership, and Bali’s stated moratorium does not prohibit its PMA registration.
